title: Human fraternity (2019)
hook: Francis and the Grand Imam of al-Azhar sign a document on fraternity in Abu Dhabi

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Year of Mercy, called Misericordiae vultus, and Holy Doors opened in cathedrals far from Rome. Your line was the door of mercy. Which work of mercy did you carry through a doorway? Day nine hundred thirty-five.

Two men sit at a table in Abu Dhabi, each with a pen. One is the pope, in white. The other is Ahmad al-Tayyeb, the Grand Imam of al-Azhar, the mosque and university in Cairo, in his own robes and turban. Between them is a document neither of them could have signed alone. They sign it, stand, and embrace. It's called the Document on Human Fraternity for World Peace and Living Together. Its first words name neither Rome nor Cairo. They name God.
screen: `TWO PENS IN ABU DHABI.` → `THE POPE AND THE GRAND IMAM.` → `IN THE NAME OF GOD.`

segments.voice: Read it slowly and it moves in four steps. First, the opening. It speaks in the name of God, who created all human beings equal in rights, duties and dignity, and called them to live together as brothers and sisters. Then it keeps going, naming the people a phrase like that can skip over: the poor, orphans and widows, refugees, the victims of war, every human life that God forbids anyone to kill. Second, what it refuses. It says plainly that religions must never be used to incite war, hatred or violence, and that God does not need to be defended by anyone killing in his name. Two religious leaders saying that together carries a different weight from either saying it alone. Third, what it asks for. Dialogue as the path. Working together as the way of acting. Understanding each other as the method. These are not grand words; they're a job description for neighbors. Fourth, what it doesn't do. It doesn't merge two faiths, or pretend Catholics and Muslims believe the same things. You heard the line from Assisi a few days ago: together, not blended. Catholics hear in it the Gospel's own words, in the Douay-Rheims, where Jesus tells his followers: "one is your master; and all you are brethren." Muslims bring their own scripture and their own reasons. Both men signed in their own names, from their own traditions. And the two signers asked that it be studied in schools, universities and places of formation, so that the young would meet it close to home.
screen: `IN THE NAME OF GOD, ALL EQUAL.` · `NEVER IN GOD'S NAME, VIOLENCE.` · `DIALOGUE, COOPERATION, UNDERSTANDING.` · `EACH FROM HIS OWN TRADITION.` · then, large: `ALL YOU ARE BRETHREN.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: get ready to greet a Muslim neighbor. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind a Muslim you know, or see often: a coworker, a shopkeeper, a parent at the school gate, a classmate. If no one comes to mind, think of any neighbor you've never really greeted. Picture saying hello properly, using their name, and waiting for the answer. A common Muslim greeting means peace be upon you, and you're welcome to say it if it's natural to you. If you pray, you can pray for them. If you don't, wish them well. The bell holds the time.
Human fraternity. The document signed in Abu Dhabi by Pope Francis and the Grand Imam of al-Azhar: all people, brothers and sisters, and never violence in God's name.
Your line: brothers and sisters. Today, greet that neighbor by name, and ask one real question about their day. Day nine hundred thirty-five.

howItsDone: Catholic dioceses and parishes take part in interreligious dialogue with local mosques and Muslim communities, sharing meals, joint service projects and study, and some mark the International Day of Human Fraternity, set by the United Nations on the anniversary of the signing.

notes: Claims rule: no date spoken. Please have both a Catholic Keeper and, if possible, an Islam Keeper read this day for fairness.

Paraphrases of the document's opening 'in the name of God', the list (the poor, orphans, widows, refugees, victims of war), the rejection of violence in God's name, and 'dialogue as the path, cooperation as the code of conduct, mutual understanding as the method': confirm against the text.

The document's controversial line on the diversity of religions being willed by God is deliberately not discussed; 'Some on both sides questioned parts of the document' is general, without a cited text; Keeper may cut.
Description of al-Azhar as 'the mosque and university in Cairo': confirm wording ('great' is descriptive of al-Azhar's name, not a ranking; Keeper may cut).
'A common Muslim greeting means peace be upon you' is a 'many' claim; Keeper to soften if needed.
International Day of Human Fraternity in howItsDone: confirm.
